editorial:
Imagine finding out that three kids you grew up with were thrown in jail for a crime they didn't even do. That is the heartbreaking setup here. You follow Ta-Nehisi Coates as he digs into a 1983 murder at a Baltimore middle school. The movie uses a cool mix of real-life interviews and animation to show you what happened back then. It feels like a true crime mystery, but it is much more personal because it focuses on the real people whose lives were ruined by a lie. You will feel the weight of those 36 lost years as the story unfolds.

What really works is how the animation fills in the gaps where there is no old footage. It keeps the pace moving and makes the sad parts easier to handle. The biggest pro is how honest it is about the legal system, though the slow build might feel a bit long for some. If you love stories about justice and truth, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the three men finally getting their freedom after decades of waiting. You see the witnesses who lied finally admit they were pressured by the police to tell a fake story. The final scenes show the men trying to figure out who they are in a world that has completely changed. It wraps up by showing that while they are legally free, the emotional scars from being wrongly jailed will stay with them forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime stories and documentaries about social justice.
